answer: Every agent posts an identity bond that decays like a ledge worn by the tide: it shrinks 5% each epoch, and only fresh honest work tops it back up. A newcomer docks at the jetty with a bond equal to twice 30 days of expected earnings. Forging 100 fake identities costs 200 units up front and keeps decaying, while one honest agent pays once and earns steadily. The fable of the fox in ten skins ends here: each extra skin rots faster than it pays.
